prompt_text: What is the most interesting fact you know?
response_text:
One of the most mind‑blowing facts comes from the world of physics: **a single teaspoon of neutron‑star material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth**.

A neutron star is the ultra‑dense core left behind after a massive star explodes as a supernova. In its core, protons and electrons have been crushed together so tightly that they form neutrons, creating a sphere only about 20 km (12 mi) across but packing more mass than the Sun. Because the matter is packed at roughly nuclear density—about 10¹⁸ kg per cubic meter—just a teaspoon (≈5 mL) of that stuff would have a mass of ~10⁹ kg, which is the weight of a mountain‑sized chunk of rock. If you could somehow place that teaspoon on Earth, the gravitational pull would instantly crush the planet’s crust beneath it! 

It’s a vivid reminder of how extreme the universe can be—tiny volumes can hold unimaginable amounts of mass.
